as_seen: *** Mary Septima, her father, her mother and her siblings *** - David, 8 October 2026
note: *** THIS IS THE ONLY IDENTIFIED LIKENESS OF MARY SEPTIMA TAYLOR THIS ARCHIVE HOLDS *** - of anyone in this family before the Cape. She is identified as the small girl at the *** lower right ***, against the knee of the seated man with full side-whiskers, who is identified as her father. *** NOBODY ELSE IN THE GROUP IS NAMED ***, and no sibling will be matched to a face here.

as_seen: *** Twelve people and a dog. *** Three male: two young men and the older man with full side-whiskers. Eight female: one markedly older, seated in a bonnet and fringed shawl; one seated in a white lace collar with the infant on her lap; six more, from a small child to grown young women. And *** one infant ***, whose sex cannot be told from the print.
note: Two ranks before a painted backdrop, with a small dog asleep on a cushion at the front left. *** THE COUNT OF FIGURES IS RELIABLE. THE COUNT OF CHILDREN IS NOT *** - see the row below, which is a correction of this archive's own first reading.

as_seen: *** WHO IS THE MOTHER, AND WHO IS A DAUGHTER. ***
note: *** DAVID IS RIGHT AND THIS ARCHIVE WAS WRONG. *** On 8 October it published that "at least eight daughters and two sons are visible", and argued from the number to the name. David then said he thought *** a grandmother or an aunt *** was in the group as well, which is the whole objection in one line. *** A GRANDDAUGHTER, A NIECE, A DAUGHTER-IN-LAW AND A NEIGHBOUR'S CHILD ALL PHOTOGRAPH IDENTICALLY. *** There are two seated adult women here and nothing in the image says which is the mother of the small girl - the one in the bonnet reads as the elder, which is exactly as consistent with a grandmother as with a mother of ten. *** A CENSUS OR A BAPTISM REGISTER COUNTS CHILDREN. A STUDIO GROUP DOES NOT. ***

as_seen: *** The picture does not prove it after all. ***
note: *** Septima *** means *** seventh ***, and this archive has carried the name as a curiosity from the beginning. A large sibling group remains the ordinary explanation - but it was already the ordinary explanation, and the photograph adds nothing to it that can be checked. *** WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: *** the 1891 census of Northam, which this archive has already read for the Brayleys, counted for the TAYLOR household instead - a census names every child, their ages and their relationship to the head, which is precisely what a photograph refuses to do.

*** INFERRED, AND ONLY INFERRED. *** Mary Septima was born *** 17 September 1884 ***. The child identified as her looks about five or six, which would put the sitting around *** 1889-1891 ***. The dress supports that range without narrowing it - high collars, and leg-of-mutton sleeves on the young woman at the right that are only beginning to swell. *** A photographer's imprint, if the mount carries one, would settle it ***, and the supplied image is cropped to the print.

The family is the *** Taylor family of Bideford and Northam, north Devon *** - Mary Septima's birth is registered at *** Bideford ***. A Devon studio is the expectation, and nothing in the image proves it.
